# What is Terraform Developer Portal?

@include "beta/tdp.mdx"

Terraform Developer Portal is an internal developer platform that allows platform teams to define golden patterns and workflows that enable a self-service experience for developers.

Terraform Developer Portal helps app developers who are responsible for creating applications and the platform engineers responsible for maintaining the infrastructure the applications run on. These roles may overlap or align differently in your organization, but Terraform Developer Portal is intended to ease the workload for any practitioner responsible for either set of tasks.

> **Hands On:** Try the [Get Started with Terraform Developer Portal](terraform/tutorials/developer-portal) collection to create a Terraform Developer Portal template and add-on definitions, then use them to deploy a sample application and its supporting infrastructure.

## How does Terraform Developer Portal work?

Terraform Developer Portal integrates deeply with HCP Terraform no-code modules to standardize infrastructure management and application deployments within your organization. This enables you to address challenges often associated with deploying and maintaining applications. Both platform engineers and application engineers can benefit from Terraform Developer Portal. 

There are several key workflows for Terraform Developer Portal: 

- **Day 0 - Set up the templates:** Platform engineers create shared templates used to deploy applications and their underlying infrastructure, and add-on definitions for common services. These standardized, shared templates and add-on definitions codify the requirements from stakeholders across the organization including security, compliance, and finance. Refer to the [Create and manage templates](/terraform/cloud-docs/developer-portal/template-create) and [Create and manage add-on definitions](/terraform/cloud-docs/developer-portal/addon-create) documentation for more information.

- **Day 1 - Set up the application:** Application developers use the templates and add-ons created by the platform engineers to deploy applications and their supporting infrastructure. The platform team maintains the templates and add-ons, which allows application developers to focus on building applications using a repeatable process on standardized infrastructure. Refer to the [Use a template to deploy and manage an application](/terraform/cloud-docs/developer-portal/template-use) and [Use an add-on to deploy supporting infrastructure](/terraform/cloud-docs/developer-portal/addon-use) documentation for more information.

- **Day 2 - Invoke actions:** Optionally, platform engineers can define Terraform actions in the no-code modules that back templates and add-ons, which application developers can invoke to interact with upstream infrastructure. For example, a Terraform action can invalidate a cache or power cycle virtual machines. For more information on Terraform actions and how to invoke them in Terraform Developer Portal, refer to the [action block reference](/terraform/language/block/action) and [Invoke actions](/terraform/cloud-docs/developer-portal/action-use) documentation.
